newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ PPI shows low production inflation in Mch qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ PPI shows low production inflation in Mch qtr.

text.p: Producer Price Index data showed low production inflation in the March quarter and the year to March, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
Input prices increased on average by 0.1 percent in the quarter and output prices rose by only 0.2 percent.
The annual increase in input prices was also only 0.1 percent, the lowest since the December 1991 quarter when a nil increase was posted, officials said.
Output prices rose 0.6 percent in the March year.
Commodity price rise contributing to the movement included oil, condensate, petroleum, sheep and lamb livestock, aluminium and finance sector charges.
Offsetting the movement were price falls for pulp, paper, wool and international airfares.

In the inputs index, industry groups contributing most to the increase were agriculture and chemicals, petroleum and plastics. Offsetting decreases came from the paper, printing and publishing sector and food, beverages and tobacco sector.

In the outputs index, increases came from the insurance and finance sector and chemicals, petroleum, and plastics. These were offset by falls in the paper, printing and publishing sector, and the trade, restaurant and hotels group.
SNZ said redeveloped indicies for mining and quarrying, electricity, gas and water and insurance and financing were included for the first time this quarter.
